definitions.explanation: The fifth grade in the {段|だん} ranking system used in martial arts, board games like {碁|ご} (Go) and {将棋|しょうぎ} (shogi), and traditional arts.
In Japanese grammar, a class of verbs whose endings shift across all five rows of the {五十音|ごじゅうおん} table when conjugated. Examples include {書|か}く, {読|よ}む, and {話|はな}す.

examples.japanese: {柔道|じゅうどう}{五段|ごだん}の{先生|せんせい}に{習|なら}った。
examples.english: I trained under a fifth-dan judo instructor.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{書道|しょどう}で{五段|ごだん}を{取得|しゅとく}した。
examples.english: My father obtained the fifth dan in calligraphy.

examples.japanese: {剣道|けんどう}の{五段|ごだん}{昇段|しょうだん}{審査|しんさ}は、{技術|ぎじゅつ}だけでなく{人格|じんかく}も{問|と}われる。
examples.english: The fifth-dan promotion exam in kendo evaluates not only technique but also character.

examples.japanese: 「{書|か}く」は{五段|ごだん}{動詞|どうし}だ。
{五段|ごだん}{動詞|どうし}は{活用|かつよう}が{多|おお}くて{覚|おぼ}えにくい。
examples.english: Godan verbs are hard to memorize because they have many conjugations.

examples.japanese: {五段|ごだん}{動詞|どうし}と{一段|いちだん}{動詞|どうし}の{違|ちが}いを{理解|りかい}することが、{日本語|にほんご}{文法|ぶんぽう}の{基礎|きそ}だ。
examples.english: Understanding the difference between godan and ichidan verbs is fundamental to Japanese grammar.

notes:
Composed of {五|ご} (five) + {段|だん} (step, grade, rank).

MEANING 1 — MARTIAL ARTS/GAMES RANKING:
- {柔道|じゅうどう}{五段|ごだん}: fifth dan in judo
- {剣道|けんどう}{五段|ごだん}: fifth dan in kendo
- {将棋|しょうぎ}{五段|ごだん}: fifth dan in shogi
- {五段|ごだん}を{取|と}る: to attain fifth dan
In most disciplines the dan ranks run from 1 ({初段|しょだん}) up to 10 ({十段|じゅうだん}), with {五段|ごだん} representing a senior practitioner.

MEANING 2 — GRAMMAR:
- {五段|ごだん}{動詞|どうし}: godan verb
- {五段|ごだん}{活用|かつよう}: godan conjugation
Named because the verb stem's final consonant takes vowels from all five rows (あいうえお) of the {五十音|ごじゅうおん} table during conjugation. Contrast with {一段|いちだん}{動詞|どうし} (ichidan verbs), whose stems stay on a single row.
